Highest-severity finding is a stub/dead-code submit handler on CreateDisputePage that silently discards form data (medium); two lower-severity i18n gaps on reachable disputes screens (FileDisputePage partial coverage, DisputeList zero coverage). All fully landable in the cloud runner — self-contained TS/i18n changes, no backend/migration/mobile dependency.

evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/disputes/pages/CreateDisputePage.tsx:29-42 — handleSubmit collects a complete CreateDisputeRequest form (respondentId, title, category, description, desiredResolution) but its ENTIRE side-effect is `await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000))` then `navigate('/disputes')`. There is NO API call — no useMutation, no api/axios call, no fetch, no @ppt/api-client import anywhere in the file. The 1-second timer is a fake-latency stub. All form data (formData state) is silently discarded; the user sees 'Submitting...' then a redirect to the disputes list and reasonably believes a dispute was filed, when nothing was persisted. The try/catch is dead (a resolving setTimeout cannot throw), so the error branch/`setError` is unreachable.

This is an orphaned stub, not the live path: the disputes route group wires `/disputes/new` to FileDisputePageRoute (frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/disputes.tsx:482 `<Route path="/disputes/new" element={<FileDisputePageRoute />} />`), which is the REAL implementation (FileDisputePageRoute.tsx imports FileDisputePage and performs the actual API side-effect at its own layer). CreateDisputePage is NOT referenced by any route file (grep for CreateDisputePage across the app returns only its own definition and the barrel re-export). However it IS publicly re-exported from features/disputes/pages/index.ts:6 (`export { CreateDisputePage } from './CreateDisputePage'`), so it is a live trap: a future author can import it from the feature barrel and mount it, shipping a form that loses every submission with no error.

Fix (pick one): (a) delete CreateDisputePage.tsx and its index.ts:6 barrel export as dead code superseded by FileDisputePage/FileDisputePageRoute; or (b) if it is meant to be a distinct entry, wire handleSubmit to the real dispute-create mutation (mirror FileDisputePageRoute's side-effect) instead of the setTimeout stub. Either way self-contained TS in the disputes feature — no backend/migration/mobile dependency, fully landable in the cloud runner.

Confidence medium (not high): the stub handler and discarded form data are directly visible, but the component is currently unrouted, so this is a latent data-loss trap / dead code rather than a confirmed live production data-loss path. Severity kept at medium rather than low because the failure mode is silent data loss on a destructive user action and the component is exported (one import away from going live).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/disputes/components/DisputeList.tsx has ZERO useTranslation usage (grep -c useTranslation = 0; no react-i18next import) yet renders a full UI of hardcoded English: h1 'Disputes' (:84), search placeholder 'Search disputes...' (:101), the three filter defaults 'All Statuses'/'All Priorities'/'All Categories' (:120,:134,:148), and the empty-state 'No disputes found.' (:165), plus action buttons. In a product whose primary locales are sk/cs/de/en (react-i18next), Slovak/Czech/German users see the entire disputes list screen in raw English.

This component is reachable in production, not dead: it is rendered by DisputesPage (features/disputes/pages/DisputesPage.tsx), which is the lazy-loaded element for the routed `/disputes` path (routes/groups/disputes.tsx:481 `<Route path="/disputes" element={<DisputesPageRoute />} />` -> DisputesPage). This is a high-traffic top-level list screen, so the untranslated strings are broadly visible.

Convention exists and is followed elsewhere in the same feature — MediationChatThread.tsx and FileDisputeDialog.tsx both use `useTranslation`/`t(...)` throughout — so DisputeList was simply never localized. Fix: add `const { t } = useTranslation()` and wrap each user-facing literal in `t('disputes.list.*', { defaultValue: ... })`, adding the keys to the sk/cs/de/en bundles. Self-contained TS/i18n change; no backend/mobile dependency — fully landable.
Confidence high: the absence of any useTranslation and the concrete hardcoded literals at the cited lines are directly visible; unambiguous i18n gap on a reachable screen.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/disputes/pages/FileDisputePage.tsx imports and uses useTranslation (partial coverage) but leaves user-facing strings hardcoded in English: the page heading `

File a Dispute

` (:193), textarea placeholder 'Brief summary of the dispute' (:351), and textarea placeholder 'Describe the dispute in detail. Include dates, times, and specific incidents (minimum 30 characters).' (:375). Because the file already localizes other strings via t(), these are inconsistency misses, not an un-started file.

This is the LIVE, routed dispute-creation screen: FileDisputePage is rendered by FileDisputePageRoute (pages/FileDisputePageRoute.tsx:11 `import { FileDisputePage } ...`), which is mounted at `/disputes/new` (routes/groups/disputes.tsx:482). So sk/cs/de/en users filing a dispute see the English heading and English form placeholders on the primary create flow.

Fix: wrap the h1 and the two placeholders in `t('disputes.file.*', { defaultValue: ... })` and add the keys to the sk/cs/de/en resource bundles, matching the t() calls already present in the file. Trivial self-contained TS/i18n change; no backend/mobile dependency — fully landable.

Confidence high: the hardcoded literals at the cited lines coexisting with existing t() usage in the same file are directly visible; unambiguous partial-i18n gap on a reachable screen. Kept low severity (+1) as a cosmetic/localization defect, not a correctness or data bug.
